title: Mehran Score — Contrast-Induced AKI Risk (PCI)
keywords: hypotension IABP CHF age anemia diabetes contrast volume creatinine eGFR
sources: Mehran R, Aymong ED, Nikolsky E, et al. A Simple Risk Score for Prediction of Contrast-Induced Nephropathy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2004;44(7):1393-1399.

changelog.change: Initial entry — the derivation-cohort points and risk categories, as an interactive calculator (the score itself was already described in prose in contrast-associated-aki).

purpose: Predicts the risk of contrast-induced AKI before a PCI — takes about 90 seconds. Score before the case, not after: it changes how much contrast you're willing to use and whether to push for a hydration protocol and IVUS-first strategy.

items.label: Hypotension (SBP < 80 for ≥ 1 h, or requiring pressors/IABP within 24 h)
Congestive heart failure (NYHA III–IV, or pulmonary edema)

interpretation.label: Low risk — ~7.5% CI-AKI
interpretation.detail: Standard periprocedural hydration is reasonable. Still minimise contrast volume and check the contrast-to-MACD ratio.

interpretation.label: Moderate risk — ~14.0% CI-AKI
interpretation.detail: Prioritise IV isotonic saline hydration (LVEDP-guided where available), minimise contrast, and consider a high-dose statin if not already on one.

interpretation.label: High risk — ~26.1% CI-AKI
interpretation.detail: LVEDP-guided hydration protocol, IVUS-first to cut contrast volume, keep the contrast/MACD ratio under 1.0, hold metformin after the case if eGFR < 30–45.

interpretation.label: Very high risk — ~57.3% CI-AKI
interpretation.detail: Maximal contrast minimisation, LVEDP-guided hydration, nephrology involvement, and an explicit conversation about deferring the procedure or staging it if clinically possible.

notes: Renal function is scored one way, not added twice — use the creatinine option only if eGFR isn't available. Derived and validated in PCI patients; applies less cleanly to non-PCI contrast studies (e.g. a straightforward CT), where the underlying risk factors still matter but the point weights weren't derived for that setting. Related: Contrast-Associated AKI — Prevention (hydration protocol, MACD, drug evidence), AKI Staging & Renal Replacement Therapy.
buildNote: Additive engine. Contrast volume (continuous, +1/100 mL) modelled as a bucketed select since the engine scores discrete options — matches the source's own point table exactly at each 100 mL boundary. Companion to the contrast-associated-aki reference module, which already carries the full prevention protocol (hydration, MACD, drug evidence).
